Ben —

Thanks for the invite. I tried to join at 11:00 AM PT but the attendee view in our calendar shows no Join button (the event description only shows the organizer's Meet link and the RSVP metadata). When I click the event it says: "You don't have access to view meeting details. Contact the organizer."

Screenshot attached (screenshot-join-missing.png). Can you either:
- reissue as a Zoom link, or
- make the organizer host so external guests can see the join controls, or
- send a simple meeting URL in the body of an email as a fallback?

We also want to include our Head of Security (Sanjay) on the session — I CC'd him.

—Jordan

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Maxwell <jordan@peakcommerce.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Dec 2025 08:25:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Quick demo scheduling — guest cannot see Join button

Lauren / Neha —

Jordan reports the guest view has no Join button and an access error. Looks like a Meet visibility/permission issue when an event is created from an external organizer or via certain cross-domain invites. Quick thoughts:

Options I can take immediately:
1) Regenerate the invite as the organizer from my GSuite account (I already tried resending ICS but that sometimes preserves the original organizer).
2) Create a Zoom meeting and replace the description with a direct Zoom link (fastest).
3) Ask Partnerships to provision a proxy host — likely overkill for a 30m demo.

Can you: 1) confirm whether we should regenerate as organizer or 2) spin a Zoom link? If we Zoom, I’ll send a new invite and include Sanjay.

I’m inclined to do Zoom fallback to avoid friction. I’ll prepare a regenerated .ics and a Zoom meeting URL.

Thanks — I’ll send the updated invite as soon as you confirm.

—Ben

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
